text:
olivia: OK curious question  who brought back the weirdest conference souvenir? :mag:
harry: I got a tiny handcrafted bottle opener shaped like a llama. fits on keychain. weirdly useful.
sam: someone put a whole pog (remember pogs?) in my swag bag. instant nostalgia. :laughing:
tara: I traded my extra T-shirt for a ceramic coffee cup from the local vendor. pack it wrapped in socks!
lem: I once packed a small glass ornamentforgot it in my carryon and it survived under a sweater. miracle.
olivia: pro tip: if you're packing fragile swag, do this snippet i learned:
```
- bubble wrap or tea towel
- put heavy items on bottom
- place fragile in middle of clothes
- label as FRAGILE on top of bag
```
travel-bot: FYI: If you purchase souvenirs for clients, list them on the expense form as "client gift" and attach receipt. Follow Redwood gift policy.
harry: tiny poll: would you rather 1) ship souvenirs home 2) carry them in carry-on 3) donate extras at airport? react with 1/2/3
sam: 1  shipping. saves the suitcase weight drama.
tara: 3 for me  free stuff for travelers is fun.
lem: also keep a small resealable bag for loose trinkets so they don't get lost.
olivia: ok I'll add "souvenir handling" to the offsite notes with a ship vs carry quick checklist. thanks for the llama stories :dromedary_camel:
